skills.trigger: Evaluating a chest X-ray in the context of high-energy blunt thoracic trauma (e.g., crush injury, deceleration) to identify signs of vascular injury.
steps: Assess the superior mediastinum for widening (typically >8 cm at the level of the aortic knob) and check for loss of definition or obscuration of the aortic knob contour.
Look for secondary signs such as deviation of the trachea or nasogastric tube to the right, depression of the left main bronchus, or apical capping (pleural cap).

Distinguish blunt aortic injury from other causes of mediastinal widening (like hematoma or lymphadenopathy) by correlating the specific location (isthmus) and mechanism; recognize that simple pneumothorax or isolated rib fractures do not explain significant mediastinal contour abnormalities.
